You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To send a letter, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Write the final postscript (2 minutes)
Step 2. Research the recipient's new office suite number (15 minutes)
Step 3. Check the letter for spelling errors (10 minutes)
Step 4. Apply a decorative wax seal (3 minutes)
Step 5. Select a high-quality linen envelope (1 minute)
Step 6. Double-check the zip code (2 minutes)
Step 7. Draft the opening salutation (5 minutes)
Step 8. Print the finalized letter (4 minutes)
Step 9. Find a working ballpoint pen (1 minute)
Step 10. Clear a space on the desk to work (5 minutes)
Step 11. Write the return address on the envelope (2 minutes)
Step 12. Buy a book of international stamps (20 minutes)
Step 13. Draft the body paragraphs (1 hour)
Step 14. Look up the current postage rates (5 minutes)
Step 15. Gather stationery supplies (10 minutes)
Step 16. Organize the finished pages in order (2 minutes)

Step 20. Ensure the ink has dried completely (10 minutes)
Step 21. Review the draft for clarity (30 minutes)

Step 23. Sign the letter by hand (1 minute)
Step 24. Fold the letter into thirds (30 seconds)
Step 25. Fact-check the claims made in the letter (45 minutes)
Step 26. Check the ink levels in the printer (5 minutes)
Step 27. Find the recipient's street address (10 minutes)
Step 28. Place the letter inside the envelope (30 seconds)
Step 29. Confirm the country's mailing format (5 minutes)
Step 30. Choose a commemorative stamp design (2 minutes)
Step 31. Clean the computer keyboard (15 minutes)
Step 32. Verify the street suffix (e.g., St vs Ave) (5 minutes)
Step 33. Proofread the final hard copy (15 minutes)
Step 34. Drop the letter in the mailbox (1 minute)
Step 35. Affix the postage stamps (1 minute)
Step 36. Insert a business card (15 seconds)
Step 37. Select a professional font (5 minutes)
Step 38. Plug in the laptop charger (30 seconds)
Step 39. Apply a small "Thank You" sticker (20 seconds)
Step 40. Search for the recipient's contact info online (10 minutes)
Step 41. Log the letter in a personal correspondence file (5 minutes)
Step 42. Print an extra copy for personal records (2 minutes)
Step 43. Moisten the envelope flap (5 seconds)
Step 44. Secure the flap with clear tape (30 seconds)
Step 45. Cite any external sources mentioned (20 minutes)
Step 46. Brainstorm the main purpose of the letter (20 minutes)
Step 47. Format the document margins (3 minutes)
Step 48. Check the current time to see if the post office is open (1 minute)
Step 49. Open the word processing software (30 seconds)
Step 50. Weigh the letter on a small scale (2 minutes)
Step 51. Find a sturdy flat surface (2 minutes)
Step 52. Outline the key points to cover (15 minutes)
Step 53. Read the letter aloud to check flow (10 minutes)
Step 54. Highlight the most important sentence (1 minute)
Step 55. Peel the backing off the stamp (10 seconds)
Step 56. Press down to seal the envelope firmly (10 seconds)
Step 57. Retrieve the paper from the drawer (2 minutes)
Step 58. Write the recipient's address on the front (3 minutes)
Step 59. Double-check the date (1 minute)
Step 60. Check for ink smudges on the paper (1 minute)
Step 61. Locate the address book (5 minutes)
Step 62. Print a mailing label (2 minutes)
Step 63. Choose between a standard or priority envelope (2 minutes)
Step 64. Check the mailbox collection times (5 minutes)
Step 65. Save the digital document (10 seconds)
Step 66. Purchase a pack of envelopes (15 minutes)
Step 67. Power on the computer (1 minute)
Step 68. Adjust the line spacing (2 minutes)
Step 69. Select the appropriate stationary color (2 minutes)
Step 70. Search for a relevant quote to include (10 minutes)
Step 71. Wipe any dust off the envelope (15 seconds)
Step 72. Write the city and state (1 minute)
Step 73. Verify the recipient's current status (10 minutes)
Step 74. Calculate the total weight (5 minutes)
Step 75. Edit the letter for brevity (20 minutes)
Step 76. Verify the page count (1 minute)
Step 77. Affix a return address label (30 seconds)
Step 78. Clear the printer paper jam (5 minutes)
Step 79. Seal the envelope with a glue stick (30 seconds)
Step 80. Check for any required customs forms (10 minutes)
Step 81. Make a digital scan of the letter (3 minutes)
Step 82. Set the letter aside for a final cooling-off period (1 hour)
Step 83. Find a comfortable chair (1 minute)
Step 84. Set the printer to high-quality mode (1 minute)
Step 85. Check that the printer is online (1 minute)
Step 86. Spray a light scent on the paper (5 seconds)
Step 87. Verify the recipient's phone number for the label (2 minutes)
Step 88. Double-check the stamp value (1 minute)
Step 89. Check for any required airmail stickers (2 minutes)
Step 90. Proofread the recipient's name one last time (1 minute)
Step 91. Walk to the end of the driveway (2 minutes)
Step 92. Look for a spare envelope (5 minutes)
Step 93. Find the roll of tape (2 minutes)
Step 94. Write the recipient's name on the envelope (1 minute)
Step 95. Check the letter for any sensitive information (10 minutes)
Step 96. Go to the post office website (5 minutes)
Step 97. Check the weather for the walk to the mailbox (2 minutes)
Step 98. Sign the back of the envelope (10 seconds)
Step 99. Raise the red flag on the mailbox (5 seconds)
Step 100. Wait for the mail carrier to arrive (4 hours)
